chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said:
Ismail held a banquet, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'You should invite the poor, so feed them until they are satisfied.'
For indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'And what falsehood starts, it will not return.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq advise regarding inviting the poor to a banquet?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) instructs Ismail to prioritize the poor at his banquet, citing the verse 'What begins falsehood does not return' (34:49) to highlight that feeding the needy is a foundational act of sincerity that establishes a lasting spiritual precedent. In Shia tradition, this emphasizes the social responsibility of the host to ensure the marginalized are not merely present but fully satisfied, reflecting the Quranic principle that true generosity begins with those in need.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman who said,
‘Ismail had a banquet, so Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘It is upon you with (inviting) the poor, so satiate them,
for Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying [34:49] and what the falsehood started, shall not return’.
en.sarwar: 16. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthaman who has said the following: “
’Isma’il prepared food for a ceremony and abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said to him, ’You must pay attention to the destitute to satisfy their hunger.
Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, says, “Falsehood is not served first or revisited for service.” [34:49]”’
